= Grammar cross-walk

// Generated by `rake reference:crosswalk` from
// lib/expressir/express/grammar/parser.rb and the Annex A snapshot.
// Do not edit by hand; the reference spec fails when this file is stale.

== Purpose

Every parsanol grammar rule is mapped to the ISO 10303-11:2004
Annex A production it implements. Divergences from the standard
grammar are classified with one of these statuses:

* `aligned` — The grammar rule implements the same-named Annex production.
* `decomposed` — The grammar rule is one piece of an Annex production that the PEG splits.
* `token` — Literal operator/delimiter token; Annex A names keywords but not punctuation.
* `lexical` — Character-class or whitespace handling inlined in the PEG (clause 7).
* `internal` — PEG-internal rule with no Annex counterpart.
* `support-code` — Handled by supporting Ruby code rather than a grammar rule.
